title: The Crab Derby, 2018
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Thirty-fourth annual. The flyer is a photo now — the girl's crab from last year, printed. Wood letters over the photo. The tradition survives as lettering.

panels.composition: Gully's. GULLY with a printout: a photo of last year's flyer, the girl's eight-legged crab, from his phone. The girl, eight, unimpressed with the photo.

balloons.text: She's got soccer. I printed last year's.
It's a crab. Blurry's fine. Hand me the pen.

image.prompt: a man in an apron holding a blurry phone printout of a child's crab drawing, an eight-year-old girl unimpressed, a thin man reaching for a pen, a dog, clean ink

panels.composition: Wood lettering over the blurry photo, the display face, the same as 1998: 34TH ANNUAL CRAB DERBY.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand lettering bold capitals over a blurry photo printout of a crab drawing

panels.composition: The girl, watching the lettering, forgetting soccer.

balloons.text: How do you make the letters the same every time.
Twenty years. You do it wrong four thousand times.

image.prompt: a small girl watching a man letter, absorbed, forgetting to leave

panels.composition: Twenty-one flyers. The twenty-first is a photo, lettered. The girl pinning it. Gully and Wood watching her reach.

image.prompt: a small girl on tiptoe pinning a lettered photo printout at the end of a long row of hand-drawn crab flyers, two men watching, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: The flyer becomes a photo. The lettering keeps the tradition. 'You do it wrong four thousand times.'
